reviews.verdict: Calls it a Cthulhu game breaking new ground, but wants summary charts for the dense rules and finds the sample adventures uneven.
Finds the system fast and fun, but the tone leans toward pulp action rather than classic Cthulhu horror.
Calls it the most complete fantasy setting he has seen and recommends it to veterans and newcomers alike.
Same content as the big book, cheaper and easier to carry; deep customization, but complex and it wears with use.
Loves Pathfinder; the pocket edition trades some readability and lay-flat use for portability and a lower price.

reviews.verdict: Ran it over three online sessions; dark, weird, easy to run, art and layout match the core book.

notes: Only a year-end favorites roundup, not a dedicated review.

reviews.verdict: A confident, accessible entry to Tolkien roleplaying; best for D&D veterans and Tolkien fans, newcomers may need guidance.
Calls it a great way to jump into the Lord of the Rings roleplaying world.

notes: Both reviews cover the 5E-based Starter Set.

reviews.verdict: Well designed and mostly fun with praised safety tools, but some moves and the Strings mechanic frustrated his group.
Calls it a great addition to current Powered by the Apocalypse games and plans to run it at cons.

notes: Reviews cover the core Thirsty Sword Lesbians book, not the Advanced Lovers & Lesbians supplement.

reviews.source: What Do I Know About Reviews?
reviews.verdict: Qualified recommendation: a beautiful book with many strengths, but know what you are getting before buying.
